mainTopic: How full and short months shape the calendar, and the dispute between רב הונא and עולא (ערכין ט׳ ע״ב)
overview: The גמרא asks what lies behind the dispute between רב הונא and עולא over how many full and short months a year may have. It answers that they follow two sides of a ברייתא about whether a leap year's extra month is thirty days or twenty-nine. A ברייתא then says ראש השנה falls only on the weekday of the עומר waving or the day after. That fits עולא, but seems to rule out רב הונא, who allows eight full months. רב הונא answers that עולא has the same problem, so the ברייתא is assigned to אחרים, who hold that the weekday moves exactly four days a year (five in a leap year). רב משרשיא shows how אחרים can still have ראש השנה on the weekday of the waving. The גמרא then explains the lesson of אחרים and why rare extra days are not counted. Finally, it brings שמואל and רבי as support for רב הונא, and answers a challenge from a נזיר vow by noting that vows follow ordinary speech. רבי's story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic issue רב הונא and עולא are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the dispute between רב הונא and עולא. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two אמוראים disagreed about how many full and short months one year may have. עולא allows eight short months but not eight full ones, and רב הונא allows eight full ones. The גמרא now wants the deeper principle behind that disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root of a dispute)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" are רב הונא and עולא, whose dispute came just before this on the דף.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens analysis of the earlier dispute between רב הונא and עולא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that explains the different positions of רב הונא and עולא

steps.title: They argue about the length of a leap year's extra month
steps.stepSummary: The dispute depends on a ברייתא: the תנא קמא says a leap year adds thirty days, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it adds a twenty-nine-day month.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about the leap year. As a ברייתא teaches: How much is added in a leap year? Thirty days. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: a month (twenty-nine days).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two אמוראים are following two sides of an older argument in a ברייתא about how long the added month in a leap year is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The length of the added month affects how the months of a leap year are counted, and so how many full or short months the year can have. רב הונא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (a 29-day added month), and עולא follows the תנא קמא (30 days).

keyTerms.meaning: Making a leap year by adding an extra month
A month; here it means a short (deficient) month of 29 days
Thirty (days)

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word "חודש" does not mean an ordinary 30-day month. He is contrasting it with the תנא קמא's "thirty", so he means a 29-day month.

phrases.english: About the leap year, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
How much is the addition of a leap year? Thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: חוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: a month.
phrases.notes: He means a short month of 29 days, one day less than the first opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעִיבּוּר שָׁנָה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on whether the leap-year month is 30 days (תנא קמא) or 29 days (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל)

steps.title: A ברייתא about which weekdays שבועות and ראש השנה fall on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as an objection: שבועות falls only on the weekday of the עומר waving, and ראש השנה falls on that weekday or the next one.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: שבועות falls only on the weekday of the waving (of the עומר), and ראש השנה falls only on the weekday of the waving or on the weekday after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge one of the opinions. This step sets up the source. The actual challenge is worked out in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר is waved on ט״ז ניסן. שבועות comes exactly seven weeks later, so it always falls on the same weekday. The ברייתא says ראש השנה, the next תשרי, can land on only two weekdays: that same one or the next one. Any opinion about the length of months must fit these two options.

keyTerms.meaning: שבועות
The day of waving the עומר, ט״ז ניסן
The day after (literally 'the night of its extra day'), meaning י״ז ניסן
Falls / occurs (on a certain day)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אִין עֲצֶרֶת חָלָה אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם הָנֵף,
phrases.english: Shavuot falls only on the day of waving,
phrases.notes: He means the same day of the week as ט״ז ניסן, when the עומר is waved.

phrases.english: and Rosh HaShana falls only

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּיוֹם הָנֵף אוֹ לְאוֹר עִיבּוּרוֹ.
phrases.english: either on the day of waving or on the night after it.
phrases.notes: "The night after" means the next day, י״ז ניסן. Again it is about the weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the positions just explained
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view of how months are set up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows ראש השנה only two possible weekdays. The גמרא will show that this fits עולא's month pattern and question whether it fits רב הונא's.

steps.title: The ברייתא works well for עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא fits עולא, who holds that a year may have eight short months but not eight full ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for עולא, who says we may make eight short months but we do not make eight full months: you can find both possibilities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a בשלמא argument: first it shows that עולא's view matches the ברייתא. This prepares the challenge against רב הונא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since עולא allows extra short months, the summer can sometimes have one more short month than usual. That gives ראש השנה two possible weekdays, just as the ברייתא says. The proof of this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view), and the next question is about the other view
Short months of 29 days
Full months of 30 days
You can find it (the case can happen)

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not end the discussion. It means 'this view fits fine', and it is the first half of a challenge against the other view.

phrases.english: It works well according to Ulla,
who says we make eight short months,
but we do not make eight full months:
you can find it.
phrases.notes: Both weekdays the ברייתא mentions for ראש השנה can happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts using the ברייתא of step 3, first showing that עולא fits
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא (by contrast, in the coming lines)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא fits עולא's month pattern, the question is whether it also fits רב הונא's.

steps.title: How each weekday comes about for עולא
steps.stepSummary: If both months in the pair are short, ראש השנה falls on the weekday of the waving. If one is full and one is short, it falls on the next weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: When both are short, it falls on the day of waving. When one is full and one is short, it falls on the night after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how עולא's view gives the two weekdays named in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From ט״ז ניסן to ראש השנה is normally 162 days when the months alternate full and short. That is 23 weeks plus one day, so ראש השנה falls on the weekday of ט״ז plus one, which is 'the night after'. If an extra short month falls in that stretch, so that two short months come together, the count is 161 days, exactly 23 weeks, and ראש השנה lands on the weekday of the waving itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Short (a 29-day month)
Full (a 30-day month)
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: For עולא, the usual pattern of alternating months puts ראש השנה one weekday after the עומר waving. An extra short month in the summer moves it back to the weekday of the waving. Both match the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Both short: on the day of waving.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מָלֵא וְאֶחָד חָסֵר — לְאוֹר עִיבּוּרוֹ.
phrases.english: One full and one short: on the night after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵיהֶן חָסֵר — בְּיוֹם הָנֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'you can find it' of step 4 by working through both cases
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two short months together give the weekday of the waving; alternating months give the next weekday. Both fit the ברייתא for עולא.

steps.title: The ברייתא does not fit רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: If רב הונא allows eight full months in a year, sometimes ראש השנה would land two weekdays after the waving, a case the ברייתא never mentions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב הונא, who says we may make eight full months, there will be times when ראש השנה falls two days after the weekday of the waving!
steps.whatsHappening: Having said the ברייתא fits עולא, the גמרא now shows why it seems not to fit רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only two options: the same weekday as the waving, or the next weekday. If רב הונא allows eight full months, which is two more than usual, one of those extra full months could fall between פסח and ראש השנה. That one extra day pushes ראש השנה from one weekday after the waving to two weekdays after it, a third option the ברייתא leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: full months of thirty days
Sometimes, there are times
Literally, on the night after the night after its extra day. Here it means two weekdays later.

phrases.english: But according to רב הונא, who says:
we may make full months,
phrases.notes: He means eight full months in one year, from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: there are times that you find it
on the night after the night after its extra day!
phrases.notes: In plain words, ראש השנה lands two weekdays after the weekday of the waving.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing the ברייתא fits עולא, the גמרא turns it against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that a year may have eight full months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eight full months mean two extra full months in the year. If one of them falls between פסח and ראש השנה, ראש השנה lands two weekdays after the waving, a case the ברייתא does not list.

steps.title: עולא has the same problem
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that even עולא allows seven full months. If the extra one falls in summer, ראש השנה would also land two weekdays later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: Does it really work for עולא? He only rules out eight full months, but seven are allowed. Sometimes the extra full month is not made in winter but in summer, and then ראש השנה falls two days after the weekday of the waving!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back. The ברייתא does not really fit עולא either, so it cannot be used against רב הונא alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא forbids eight full months but allows seven, which is one more than normal. If that extra full month falls in the summer, between פסח and ראש השנה, the same two-day shift happens. So the ברייתא is hard for both views, and it can no longer settle their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it really work out well?
Winter
Summer

phrases.english: רב הונא can say to you:
And does it work out well for עולא?
It is eight full months that we do not make,
but seven we do make.
With seven, sometimes we do not make the extra one in the winter
but we make it in the summer,
and then it is on the night after the night after its extra day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: וּלְעוּלָּא מִי נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack in step 6 by showing that עולא faces the same difficulty.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא supports עולא over רב הונא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עולא's allowance of seven full months produces the same two-day case.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא does not allow only six full months. He rules out eight, so seven, one extra, is still possible.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא follows אחרים, who say the weekday moves exactly four days each year, or five in a leap year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whose view is this ברייתא? It is אחרים, as it was taught: אחרים say that between one שבועות and the next, and between one ראש השנה and the next, there are only four days of difference, and in a leap year, five.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the ברייתא fits neither רב הונא nor עולא, the גמרא tries to match it to a different opinion, that of אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shift of exactly four weekdays each year means the year always has 354 days, with full and short months alternating perfectly. So אחרים never allow any extra full months. That would remove the two-day problem raised against both רב הונא and עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
'Others', a תנא whose opinion is quoted under this name
שבועות
A leap year, with an extra month

phrases.english: Rather, whose view is this?
It is אחרים, as it was taught:
אחרים say:
There is no difference between one שבועות and the next,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: and no difference between one ראש השנה and the next,
except four days only,
phrases.notes: Four days of the week: the date lands four weekdays later the next year.

phrases.english: and if it was a leap year, five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָא מַנִּי? אֲחֵרִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since both רב הונא and עולא face the problem, the גמרא assigns the ברייתא to a third opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must fit either רב הונא or עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows אחרים, who hold that the months always alternate, so there is never a two-day shift.

steps.title: אחרים cannot explain the 'day of waving' case
steps.stepSummary: In the end, according to אחרים, ראש השנה could never fall on the weekday of the waving, yet the ברייתא lists that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, according to אחרים, you never find ראש השנה falling on the weekday of the waving!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתא follows אחרים, because it leaves another part of the ברייתא without an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With months that always alternate, the gap from the waving to ראש השנה never changes. Under אחרים, ראש השנה could never land on the same weekday as the waving. But the ברייתא clearly says it sometimes does. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, after all
The day the עומר is waved, the 16th of ניסן

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two options (the same weekday as the waving, or the next weekday) do not fit cleanly with רב הונא, עולא, or אחרים. Every candidate so far has run into a problem.

phrases.english: In the end, according to אחרים,
on the day of waving, you do not find it!
phrases.notes: He means ראש השנה never falls on the weekday of the עומר waving.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, לַאֲחֵרִים, בְּיוֹם הָנֵף לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 8 that the ברייתא follows אחרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With perfect alternation, ראש השנה can never fall on the weekday of the waving, but the ברייתא says it can.

steps.title: How a leap year lets ראש השנה match the day of the waving
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers the question from Step 9. In a leap year whose added month has thirty days, one full month after פסח is made short. This can make ראש השנה fall on the same weekday as the waving of the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: Take a leap year where the added month was thirty days. Remove a month after פסח to balance that extra month, and you will find ראש השנה falling on the same weekday as the waving.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא saves the ברייתא from the question in Step 9. He shows a real case where, even according to אחרים, ראש השנה lands on the weekday of the waving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thirty-day added month would push the weekday too far. According to אחרים, a leap year moves the weekday by exactly five days, so one full month after פסח must become short to balance the extra full month. When that happens, ראש השנה falls on the same weekday as the waving, which is the case the ברייתא lists.

keyTerms.meaning: A leap year, which has an extra month added
The extra month that is added to make a leap year
Take away, remove (from the count)
The day the עומר is waved, on the 16th of ניסן

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
For example, where it was a leap year,
and the month added to the year was thirty days,
take away a month to match a month,
phrases.notes: He means: make one month after פסח short, to balance the extra full month added before פסח.

phrases.english: so that you find it on the day of the waving.
phrases.notes: "It" is ראש השנה, falling on the same weekday as the waving of the עומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה שָׁנָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by giving a case that fits אחרים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a specific case (a leap year with a thirty-day added month) where the listed outcome can happen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to אחרים, ראש השנה could never fall on the weekday of the waving
steps.terutzMaskana: In a leap year with a full added month, one later month is made short, and ראש השנה falls on the weekday of the waving

steps.title: Why did אחרים need to give a fixed count
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks רבא what אחרים were trying to teach by giving a fixed number of weekday shifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: Did אחרים come to teach us a count of days?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה asks what the point of the statement of אחרים is. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the months simply go full, short, full, short, anyone could work out the count. So why did אחרים need to say it? The question looks for the real lesson hidden in their statement.

keyTerms.meaning: A count, a number
To teach us, to let us know

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
Did אחרים come to teach us a count?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending the ברייתא to asking about the purpose of the statement of אחרים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new lesson the fixed count of אחרים is meant to teach

steps.title: Months may follow a fixed order, not only the sighting of the moon
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that אחרים teach that we do not have to set the new month only by seeing the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: we do not require that the month must be sanctified according to the sighting of the moon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the lesson behind the statement of אחרים. Their fixed count shows that a new month may be set by the fixed order of months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By giving a fixed pattern, אחרים show that בית דין does not have to wait until the moon is seen. If the order says a month should be short, the next month may be declared even if the moon was not seen.

keyTerms.meaning: To sanctify, meaning to declare the start of a new month
Based on the sighting (of the new moon)
We do not require

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that setting the calendar by a fixed order is acceptable, and not only by witnesses who saw the moon.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that we do not require that it is a מצוה
to sanctify the month according to the sighting.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחרים teach that a new month may be declared by fixed order, without needing to see the moon

steps.title: The extra days that build up over the years
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects that the moon's month is a bit longer than twenty-nine and a half days. Over time this adds extra days, so the weekday cannot always move by the same fixed amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: But there is the day that comes from the extra hours, and the day that comes every thirty years!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the fixed count of אחרים. He points out extra days that build up over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moon's month is slightly longer than twenty-nine and a half days. The small leftovers add up into an extra day every few years and another extra day every thirty years. So the weekday shift cannot always be exactly four or five days.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, he challenges it
The day made up from extra hours that add up
The extra day that builds up over thirty years

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it:
But there is the day of the hours,
phrases.notes: The extra hours beyond twenty-nine and a half days add up to a whole day every few years.

phrases.english: and the day of thirty years!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא וְהָאִיכָּא יוֹמָא דְּשָׁעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge against the fixed count of אחרים
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of אחרים that the weekday always moves exactly four days, or five in a leap year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Extra time builds up into added days, so the shift cannot always be fixed

steps.title: Days that do not come every year are not counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that these extra days do not happen every year, so the ברייתא did not count them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it does not happen every year, it is not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא's challenge. The ברייתא only counts what happens every year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra days are real, but they come only once in a while. The rule of אחרים describes the regular yearly pattern, so rare extra days are left out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is not present
He does not count it

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רב הונא about the length of the year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that שמואל also holds like רב הונא. שמואל says a lunar year can be up to 356 days long, which means it can have eight full months.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל also holds like רב הונא, since שמואל said: A lunar year is not less than 352 days and not more than 356 days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument between רב הונא and עולא. It brings שמואל as support for רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A year that alternates full and short months has 354 days, with six full months. If a year can reach 356 days, it must have eight full months, which is exactly what רב הונא allows. So שמואל's numbers back up רב הונא against עולא, who allows at most seven.

steps.title: How the year can be 356, 352, or 354 days
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's statement explains its own numbers. Two full months make 356 days, two deficient months make 352, and one of each makes 354.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If both are full, the year has 356 days. If both are deficient, it has 352. If one is full and one is deficient, it has 354.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing שמואל's statement by showing exactly how the different year lengths come about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal lunar year switches between full months of 30 days and deficient months of 29 days, for 354 days in total. If two months that are usually deficient are both made full, two days are added (356). If two usually-full months are both made deficient, two days are lost (352). Since 356 needs extra full months, this shows that שמואל allows eight full months in one year.

steps.confusionAlert: The numbers 'six, two, four' are short for 356, 352 and 354. The text only says the last digit because the 'three hundred fifty' part is already understood.

steps.title: Challenge from a נזיר vow 'like the days of the moon'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who vows to be a נזיר 'like the days of the moon' counts 354 days. If a lunar year can sometimes be 356 days, why not count that?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: If someone says, 'I am a נזיר like the days of the sun,' he counts 365 days of נזירות, like the number of days in a solar year. If he says, 'like the days of the moon,' he counts 354 days, like the number of days in a lunar year. But if what you say is true, sometimes you find a lunar year of 356 days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a ברייתא about a נזיר vow to challenge שמואל's claim that a lunar year can have 356 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the lunar year as exactly 354 days. If a lunar year could really reach 356 days, the ברייתא should have said so, or at least allowed for it. So the ברייתא seems to show that a lunar year is always 354 days.

steps.title: Vows follow how people normally talk
steps.stepSummary: Vows are understood by everyday speech. When people say 'a lunar year,' they mean a typical year, which is 354 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: With vows, we follow the way people talk, and people mean most years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that the ברייתא is about the meaning of a vow, not about astronomy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say that a lunar year is always 354 days. It only tells us what a person means when he says 'like the days of the moon.' Ordinary people mean a normal year, and most years have 354 days. So a rare 356-day year can still exist.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that vows follow ordinary speech is a basic principle across all the laws of נדרים.

steps.title: רבי made nine deficient months
steps.stepSummary: Support that רבי held like רב הונא. רבי once made nine deficient months in a year, and yet the new moon was still seen on time, which surprised him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי also held like רב הונא, as a ברייתא teaches: There was an incident where רבי made nine deficient months, and the new moon was seen at its proper time. רבי was amazed and said: We made nine deficient months, and the new moon was seen at its proper time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about רבי as support for רב הונא, who allows a year to have eight full months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי made nine short months in one year, far more than the usual six. He expected the calendar to drift away from the moon, so he was surprised that the new moon still appeared right on schedule. His son's answer in the next step, which continues on the next amud, shows how this story supports רב הונא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון suggests a leap year explains it
steps.stepSummary: רבי's son רבי שמעון suggests that a leap year may explain why the new moon still came on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון, son of רבי, said before him: Perhaps it was a leap year?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון offers an answer to his father's puzzle, and the explanation continues in the next line of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי could not understand how nine short months still matched the moon. His son suggests that a leap year, with its extra month, could have balanced things out. The full explanation is completed in the text that follows.
